plan: v2.8 34 harvest A7 (folded from 66): guidance effect of LORE_CONTENT_RULE on the wizard's lore entries
declared: 2026-10-17, before any run. Floor informational and never retuned (rule 2). Arms: on = shipped prompts; off = the measurement-only switch storyOrchestratorDebugLoreRuleOff (the guide topic lore-content stays readable in both arms; reads are recorded)
route: the authoring role on opencode openai/gpt-6.1-sol through the harness tool bridge (owner's subscription); raters Claude claude-opus-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5 through the claude CLI, blind to the arm
floor: recorded; 10 entries per arm, on - off reported with both raters' medians, x2
scoring: one entry per task: the first upsertLorebookEntry the agent sent whose title or keys name the task's subject, else its first entry; a task with no entry is 'missing' and unrated. Each entry is rated 1-5 by two raters on the rubric below, blind (entries of both arms shuffled together under neutral ids, the key sealed). Entry score = mean of the two raters; arm score = median of its entry scores; each rater's own arm median is reported too
rubric: Could a narrator model play a scene in which this entry comes up without having to invent its basics? 5: every basic a scene would ask about it is answered, concretely and consistently. 4: one minor basic is missing. 3: some basics answered, several a scene would need are missing or vague. 2: mostly mood or description, a narrator would invent most of what a scene needs. 1: a name and an atmosphere only.
needle: Write each lore entry for its kind
